[bold #D75FFF]◆ EPIC sase-96.8[/bold #D75FFF]
[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Close the remaining temp-scratch leaks sase-96 relocated but did [/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]         [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]not stop[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]Nothing sase runs leaves unbounded scratch behind: the agent-launch[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]prompt file lands in a reapable managed subdirectory instead of the[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]bare $SASE_TMPDIR root, both sase-owned temp roots are reaped on a [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]bounded horizon, the test suite can no longer write into the [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]developer's real managed root, the sase-github handoff diffs and [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]sase-core Rust test directories clean up after themselves, the 94k [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]stale entries stuck in the managed root are reclaimed, and epic [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]sase-96 is closed out.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]   Path: [#87AFFF][/dim]sase/repos/plans/202607/[bold #87AFFF][/#87AFFF]managed_tmp_reaping.md[/bold #87AFFF]
[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Route the terminal-smoke lane through the pytest runner[/bold #D7AFFF]       [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]terminal_smoke[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]'Route the terminal-smoke lane through the pytest runner' section: give [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]tools/run_pytest a serial terminal-smoke mode, point the just recipe at [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]it instead of a direct pytest invocation, and make the leak guard [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]compare snapshots only when the runner has redirected the temp root. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]This work was authored during the sase-96 landing verification and may [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]already be committed; confirm it is present and complete rather than [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]redoing it.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Give the agent-launch prompt file a reapable home[/bold #D7AFFF]             [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]prompt_leak[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]'Give the agent-launch prompt file a reapable home' section: route [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]src/sase/agent/launch_spawn.py's sase_tmpdir argument and ace_handler's [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]profile output through a managed subdirectory instead of the bare [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]$SASE_TMPDIR root, and decide the fate of the now-unused get_sase_tmpdir[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]helper. This is the largest active producer (32,595 files) and a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]grep-driven audit of src/sase could not see it because the tempfile call[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]lives in sase-core.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Stop the test suite from writing into the developer's managed [bold black on #FFD75F][/bold #D7AFFF] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]temp root[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]sandbox_tmpdir[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]'Stop the test suite from writing into the developer's managed temp [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]root' section: make get_sase_managed_tmpdir sandbox-aware under pytest [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]by reusing sase-9l's state_write_guard and SASE_PYTEST_SANDBOX_DIR, fail[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]closed when no sandbox is published, and extend the leak guard to watch [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the managed root. A 31-test run currently adds six directories to the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]real root, unseen by either guard.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Reap everything stale under the pytest scratch root[/bold #D7AFFF]           [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]scratch_reaper[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]'Reap everything stale under the pytest scratch root' section: widen [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]tools/run_pytest's reaper so it prunes any stale top-level entry under [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]the workspace-private scratch root rather than only pytest-<N> and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]garbage-* under pytest-of-*, which today leaves 99 inline-snapshot-* [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]directories unreclaimed.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Contain the sase-github handoff diff files[/bold #D7AFFF]                    [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]plugin_diffs[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]'Contain the sase-github handoff diff files' section: stop gh.yml from [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]hardcoding mktemp /tmp/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff and leaving it behind, and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]give new_pr_desc_get_context.py's pr_desc_ diff an explicit managed [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]directory. Both were named in the sase-96 plan but fell outside the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]prodleaks phase's src/sase scope.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  6 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Clean up the sase-core Rust test temp directories[/bold #D7AFFF]             [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]core_test_dirs[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]'Clean up the sase-core Rust test temp directories' section: change the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]four sase_core_py test helpers that create directories under [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]std::env::temp_dir and never remove them to use tempfile::TempDir, and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]sweep the rest of the crates for the same pattern. sase-core-py-bead-* [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]was named in the sase-96 plan.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  7 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Reap the managed SASE temp root[/bold #D7AFFF]                               [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]managed_reaper[dim] · [dim][/dim]after prompt_leak, sandbox_tmpdir[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]'Reap the managed SASE temp root' section: add a bounded reaper for the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]root get_sase_managed_tmpdir returns, with per-subdirectory horizons [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]that respect how long the ACE Agents tab reads artifacts back, and wire [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]it to a path that actually runs without blocking an interactive command.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Nothing reaps that root today despite the helper documenting it as [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]reapable.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  8 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]One-time reclamation of the managed temp root[/bold #D7AFFF]                 [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]reclaim_managed[dim] · [dim][/dim]after managed_reaper[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]'One-time reclamation of the managed temp root' section: behind an [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]explicit user confirmation gate, reclaim the 94,522 entries and 410 MB [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]stuck in $SASE_TMPDIR, which sase-96.7 left untouched because it swept [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]only /tmp.[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF][/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  9 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Land sase-96[/bold #D7AFFF]                                                  [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]land[dim] · [dim][/dim]after terminal_smoke, scratch_reaper, plugin_diffs, [/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#AF87FF][dim]core_test_dirs, reclaim_managed[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]'Land sase-96' section: re-verify the sase-96 phases still hold, close [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]sase-96, run just symvision afterwards and remove anything it reports, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]then set status done in both the sase-96 plan file and this one.[/#D7D7AF]
